findings.description: The request line is parsed with istringstream extraction, which collapses space runs and treats TAB as a separator, and the only grammar check is the three-token extraction plus token(method). So GET  /hello.txt, TAB-delimited, leading-space and trailing-space forms are all accepted 200 and re-emitted as a normal single-space line: accepted but identical, negative for smuggling. The delta appears only when proxy_pass carries a URI and the target is rebuilt from the decoded path, where a %20 becomes a raw space and the upstream split() re-cuts the line to four tokens. On the plain form the RCE survives; when the exec route is not the first segment (GET /exec/a%20exec?cmd=whoami to GET /a exec?cmd=whoami) the displaced query lands as token 4 and EXEC comes back empty, so an accepted shape silently kills a working RCE. Precondition: a rewriting proxy_pass.
findings.title: The istringstream parser accepts double space, tab, leading and trailing space but normalises them back to three tokens, so a decoded space in a rewritten proxy_pass target is what actually shifts the downstream token count

limitations: All RCE is RCE on the upstream host
